Content identity rule: SHA-256 of one UTF-8 line 'relative_path<TAB>sha256<TAB>bytes<LF>' per entry, in item_id order. The manifest's SHA-256 pins the
frozen record; the content identity pins the folder, independent of timestamps and
formatting. Both are recorded in `data/manifest.json` under `external_corpora`.

## An observation from one file, not a corpus property

Kaiyuan Liao opened one file in the folder, before this inventory, and it appeared off-topic: about urban surface water in Wuhan. This is an observation from one file, reported by Kaiyuan, not a property of the corpus; which file it was is not recorded, and this inventory opened no file to check. Consequence: M4-WP1's deterministic sample should expect off-topic items.

## Ids and reproducibility

- LIT-NNNNNN assigned once, in code-point order of the POSIX relative path; frozen thereafter. A re-run verifies against the frozen manifest and fails if the path set or any file's bytes changed.
- Byte-level reads only, for SHA-256 and size. No file is decoded, parsed, rendered or inspected; no filename is read for meaning. Symlinks are not followed; archives are not expanded.
- Every entry carries at least relative path, extension, bytes and SHA-256, and a
  stable id suitable for a later bounded M4-WP1 sample drawn by rule.
- No entry carries a hazard group, a topic, a title, or any other reading. The collection
  query assigns nothing to any individual file.

## Sophia

The corpus is **not** on Sophia. A later package will transfer it out of band, with this
manifest as the verification gate --- the same pattern as `FullData.csv` (D-005). See
`docs/SOPHIA_RUNBOOK.md`.
